clue.text: In America a girl on route to NY theatreland

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman or girl
a way is a route or road

explanation.surface: An American girl sets off along the road to New York's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' flags that BROAD is US slang; 'on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the New York street whose theatres give the district its name.

clue.text: Spirit — and what it often flows from

definitions.meaning: British slang for courage or nerve
liquor (spirit) is poured from a glass container

explanation.definitionFit: Courage is called nerve or pluck in British slang, and a spirit such as whisky is poured from its glass vessel.

clue.text: Old atomic power unit turns up in Canada

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words atomic power unit are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for atomic, as in A-bomb
the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: An outdated nuclear power station surfaces somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses A WATT to TTAWA, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: Old German artist unusually rude about front of Reichstag

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
unusually signals that the letters of rude are arranged in an uncommon order
front of picks out the first letter of the word Reichstag

explanation.surface: An old German painter behaves rudely near the front of the Berlin parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns RUDE into DURE, which goes 'about' R, the 'front of Reichstag'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a renowned painter and engraver of the German Renaissance.

clue.text: A bounder beginning to egg on my school

parts.note: a cad is an old-fashioned word for a bounder, a dishonourable man

indicators.note: beginning to selects the opening letter of the word egg

explanation.surface: A rogue starts urging on my old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the pieces simply run A, CAD, E, MY.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a type of school, especially in the UK state system.

clue.text: Lion born on small island gained initially about a ton

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born in genealogies
I is a short form of island

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word gained

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A lion born on a little island put on about a ton in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word; the pieces run B, I, G, CA, T in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions, tigers and leopards are the large wild felines known collectively by this phrase.

clue.text: Do it in car perhaps, with a flashing light

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the words do it in car, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Signal your turn in the car with a blinking lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal; 'with' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's blinker is the flashing lamp that shows which way the driver will turn.

clue.text: How mince is chopped up to make Chinese dish

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces, so the letters of how mince are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A recipe line explaining how minced meat is chopped for a Chinese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese-style dish of stir-fried noodles.

clue.text: Training time needed on lute movement — lots of time

indicators.note: movement signals the letters of lute shifting into a new order

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Learning the lute takes time and practice, and a great deal of time at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' anagrams LUTE to UTEL; 'needed on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guidance given by a tutor.

clue.text: Strange ritual about to yield period of intensive tuition

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the scrambled letters surround the little word to
strange signals the letters of ritual arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An odd ceremony is about to give way to a study session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' makes TURIAL from RITUAL, which goes 'about' TO; 'yield' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a session of concentrated teaching given to one student or a small group.

clue.text: Clever lady, without taking sides, dispersed riot

indicators.note: without its sides means the word lady loses its first and last letters
dispersed means scattered, so the letters of riot are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever woman stays neutral as a riot breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without taking sides' leaves AD of LADY; 'dispersed' turns RIOT into ROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted.

clue.text: Deliberately do without sleep on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed beneath, so sleep sits under Sunday

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to forgo a Sunday lie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: KIP is British slang for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to miss or omit it on purpose.

clue.text: Petty officers and seamen drop the cards

parts.note: to lower is to drop or let down
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Sailors of the lower ranks put down their playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: On a warship the lower deck is the collective term for ratings below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratings of a navy, as opposed to commissioned officers, are known by this collective term.

clue.text: Arrived and left in Bedouin's transport

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turned up and then departed on a desert nomad's mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert nomads traditionally ride this humped animal.

clue.text: Fight with France, yes?

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A question about whether to join a battle alongside the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; AY, as in 'the ayes have it', means yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or noisy skirmish.

clue.text: Old parliamentarian has several drinks with the leader

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
the head is the leader or chief

explanation.surface: A former MP orders a lot of drinks with the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were supporters of Parliament in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War the Puritan supporters of Parliament against the King bore this nickname.

clue.text: Putting balls away in shed, sort of

definitions.meaning: in snooker or pool, sending balls into pockets
a gardener's outbuilding for raising plants in pots goes by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Sinking balls into pockets in snooker has this name, and a garden outbuilding for plant pots is a potting shed.

clue.text: Cricket statistician is outside the church — it's a hot day

indicators.note: is outside means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a scorer records the runs and wickets in a cricket match
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The cricket scorer stands outside the church on a sweltering day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorcher is informal for a very hot day.

clue.text: Makes mincemeat of counters

indicators.note: making mincemeat of something chops it up, so the letters of counters are minced into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing an opponent's game pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: as a definition (beats soundly) and as an instruction to chop up COUNTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat them heavily, which is what making mincemeat of them means.

clue.text: About to wake up and make merry

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about
to rouse is to wake up

explanation.surface: Someone just about to wake up and start celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and revel noisily.

clue.text: Leave previous partner to sit on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on means placed above, so the ex goes over it

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Telling a former partner to leave and sit on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart.

clue.text: Several hundred from Rome on ship without light

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
Noah's ark is the classic ship of crossword clues

explanation.surface: Several hundred Romans aboard a ship sail in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark means lacking illumination.

clue.text: Remove first piece of pipe inside exhaust

indicators.note: inside means the letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: to delete is to remove

indicators.note: first piece of picks out the opening letter of the word pipe

explanation.surface: Instructions to take the first section of pipe out of a car exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a noun from a car; it is the verb meaning use up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or drain a supply.

clue.text: Goes over to grab publicity for the Ancient Mariner

indicators.note: to grab means to seize and hold, so the reversed word encloses the other piece
over means turned over, so the word goes is read backwards

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: An old sailor goes over to seize some publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns GOES into SEOG, which grabs AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old, experienced sailor, like Coleridge's ancient mariner.

clue.text: Support cricket side and remain behind

parts.note: a stay is a prop or support
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket fan supports the team and stays on afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (or leg) side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to continue somewhere after others leave.

clue.text: Plump for drinks -it's part of boxing

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for a group
one of the timed periods in a boxing bout

explanation.definitionFit: Rotund figures, a pub order for everyone, and a three-minute boxing period all share this word.

clue.text: Little devil let men inside piece of equipment

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: inside means the word men goes within the word let

explanation.surface: A mischievous child lets some men into the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool or utensil.

clue.text: Competition the day before not void

parts.note: eve is the day before an ..., as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: void means emptied, so the word not loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A contest the previous day that still counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'void' empties NOT to NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a contest in a sports programme.

clue.text: English painter abandons new ball game

indicators.note: abandons means gives up, so the painter's name drops a letter

parts.note: David Hockney is a celebrated English painter

explanation.surface: A famous English artist gives up a fresh ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N from HOCKNEY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball.

clue.text: For a week say, including flat, five hundred

indicators.note: including means the word say holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: taken as written
even means flat or level
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Booking a flat for a week at around five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual signal that an example follows, but here it is taken literally as part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven-day describes something lasting a full week.

clue.text: Live in some obscure side street

indicators.note: some means only part of the words obscure side is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Living somewhere down an obscure back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the letters run across obscuRE SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell in a place.

clue.text: A writer to go after America's military command?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to tag on is to follow along behind

explanation.surface: A journalist chasing the US armed forces headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition names a building standing for the command.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense, standing for its military leadership.
